description:
An area of heathland and moors, teeming with insects (honeybees) and with a gentle breeze rustling through the heather bushes.
About the picture You are looking out over an open nature reserve in the Kampina, where there would normally be water in the Zandbergse Vennen. Instead, you see a wide, dry plain: the ground is light in colour and consists of hard, cracked earth, as if the fen had completely dried up. The cracks run like thin lines across the surface, giving the scene a barren and fragile character. Only in the far right-hand corner can a little water from one of the fen areas still be seen.

🌿 Features of the Kampina and Zandbergse vennen In the heart of the Kampina, where silence is still the norm, the Zandbergse Vennen lie like glistening eyes in the landscape. These small, shallow pools form a mosaic of wet heathland, sphagnum moss fields and open water, and give a glimpse of what Brabant looked like before agriculture and development transformed the landscape. The ponds were formed by natural leaching in the sandy soil, creating nutrient-poor, clear waters in which unique plants and animals thrive. Around the banks grow sphagnum moss, lavender heath and the delicate round-leaved sundew, a carnivorous plant that has adapted to the harsh conditions. Between the tufts of purple moor grass and gorse thickets lies a transitional zone that takes on a different colour in every season: fresh green in spring, warm gold in summer and deep reddish-brown in autumn. The Zandbergse Vennen are a refuge for animals that have become rare elsewhere. Dragonflies such as the white-faced darter skim across the water’s surface, whilst moor frogs and pool frogs hide amongst the sphagnum moss. In the early morning, you can hear the little grebe, a small waterbird that likes to linger in the quiet ponds. Tree larks breed on the surrounding heathland, and the mysterious nightjar sometimes glides over the fields of purple-flowering plants. Unfortunately, I realised today that the ponds are almost completely dry (see photo) due to climate change, which is now making the climate here resemble that of the south of France in the 1960s.
Zandbergse vennen July 2018. only 8 years earlier.
